extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists and readers/contributors of the Philosophical Transactions (Royal Society)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for designing, reporting, and interpreting experimental natural-philosophy investigations (17th-century Royal Society style). Emphasizes controls, verification of apparatus/conditions, avoidance of artefacts, and reliance on evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid invoking unsupported hypothetical entities
rubrics_metrics.description: “has recourse to the action of a matter, of whose existence there has never been any kind of evidence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not explain observed phenomena by positing new substances or forces without direct evidence; prefer explanations based on known, evidenced principles (e.g., attraction/cohesion) rather than ad hoc hypothetical matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware experimental artefacts introduced by the method
rubrics_metrics.description: “The forcible inflation here resorted to is a great objection to deducing any conclusions from these experiments, which indeed appear to be of little value.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a procedure (e.g., forcible inflation, excessive drying, harsh manipulation) can itself produce the observed effect, do not draw firm conclusions; design experiments to avoid or control for artefacts and note when methods may confound interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify apparatus/conditions with multiple independent checks
rubrics_metrics.description: “he did assure himself... by finding that there came out no more air through the pump, as by other more certain marks.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm critical experimental conditions (e.g., degree of vacuum) using several independent indicators rather than a single check, and report how verification was achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for dissolved gases / prepare reagents appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: “with water purged of air it did the effect as well as without the recipient.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When hypotheses depend on presence/absence of gases (or other dissolved constituents), remove or standardize them (e.g., purge water of air) and report such preparations to isolate causal factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use variant conditions and comparative trials to isolate causes
rubrics_metrics.description: (plate adhesion and related experiments) He tried plates joined in vacuum, put spirit of wine between plates, and compared behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary one condition at a time (different interstitial fluids, presence/absence of air, tube lengths, etc.) and compare results to identify which factor produces the effect; include such variants in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report quantitative apparatus dimensions and measured outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifics such as tube heights (e.g., 75 inches), syphon leg lengths (8 inches), aperture sizes (two lines), and timed intervals are given in the accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric details of apparatus and quantitative measurements (lengths, apertures, heights, times) so results are reproducible and interpretable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicate trials and record timing/variation across trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Viper experiments report multiple animals, repeated trials, and times-to-death (minutes) for each trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform repeated trials, document variation and precise timings of effects, and report the number of replicates to support reliability and allow assessment of consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include proper controls, including sham/negative controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: puncturing with thorns or pins to show wounding alone does not cause the observed poisoning; testing dried vs fresh gum from viper gums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments with negative and sham controls that mimic mechanical injury or other non-specific effects to rule out confounding causes; compare treated and control groups explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek independent corroboration and use appropriate observational tools
rubrics_metrics.description: “I am pretty well assured by my own, and also by my ingenious friend Dr. Johnson's more accurate microscopical observations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate findings via independent observers and appropriate instruments (e.g., microscopy); cite independent confirmation when available to strengthen claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainties, scruples, and methodological limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors acknowledge remaining scruples about their explanations and note methodological limitations in experiments and interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State candidly what aspects of an explanation remain uncertain, what possible objections exist, and what limitations the methods impose on interpretation; avoid overstating conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer explanations consistent with established properties; require strong evidence for extraordinary claims
rubrics_metrics.description: “Philosophers can employ their time better... than by reading accounts of experiments said to yield results not reconcilable with the known and immutable properties of natural bodies.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat extraordinary or anomalous results with caution: ensure they are robustly verified and reconciled with known properties (or provide compelling evidence for revision). Avoid accepting claims that conflict with established knowledge without substantial supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contemporary, robust analytical/mathematical methods where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentary noting intricate algebraical expressions were superseded by the easier method of fluxions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ the best available analytical or mathematical techniques to simplify, clarify, or supersede overly complex methods, and state where newer methods improve interpretation or calculation.
